title: What can you say about zinc in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 5 wordings for zinc; the strongest is "Supports normal immune function" (strong, 0.7-50 mg elemental zinc a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Shortens colds, or protects against colds".

supported_wordings.why: Listed by Health Canada and authorized in the EU after EFSA review; ODS describes zinc's role in immune function.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Health Canada: 0.7-50 mg a day for adults 19 and older (0.7-25 mg from picolinate; 0.7-34 mg at age 18). ODS sets the adult upper limit at 40 mg a day. The EU claim applies to products that are at least a 'source' of zinc.
supported_wordings.form: Any zinc form on Health Canada's list, counted as elemental zinc

sources.name: Commission Regulation (EU) No 432/2012, list of permitted health claims

supported_wordings.dose_warning: Above 40 mg a day of zinc is over the ODS upper limit for adults, and 50 mg or more over weeks can lower copper absorption. Health Canada's range runs to 50 mg; the claim's support stands.

supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists healthy bones, hair, nails and skin, and the EU authorizes maintenance of normal skin, hair, nails and bones.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Shortens colds, or protects against colds
wordings_to_avoid.why: Names a disease. ODS reports a 2024 Cochrane review finding zinc may cut cold duration by about 2 days once a cold has started, and makes little or no difference in avoiding colds; ODS also notes zinc is sold in over-the-counter cold remedies, which are drugs.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Treats low testosterone or erectile dysfunction
wordings_to_avoid.why: Names medical conditions; the supported wording is maintaining normal testosterone levels.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Fights viruses, or protects against COVID-19

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
